rubrics.justification: Generally consistent with a good-quality expanded/hatching blastocyst and visible ICM, but it overstates certainty about TE uniformity, nuclear features, and active herniation mechanics that are not clearly discernible from this single image.

Integrates age, ovarian reserve, tubal factor, prior outcomes, sperm quality, BMI, and endometrium well with embryo quality, though it somewhat overinterprets prior outcomes as a recurrent implantation failure pattern.

Reasoning is structured and mostly logical, with probability estimates tied to embryo quality and history; minor issues include labeling biochemical pregnancy plus miscarriage as RIF-like and inferring diminished reserve too strongly from one retrieval.

Much is guideline-concordant (eSET, avoiding bed rest, caution on heparin/intralipids), but recommendations such as routine aspirin, Medrol, ERA/ReceptivaDx after this history, and embryo banking are more controversial or not broadly guideline-supported.
Provides clear practical next steps for transfer management and contingency planning, though some suggested adjuncts and investigations may be more speculative than standard-of-care.
